Subject: Sales discovery follow-up — model fit & next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciate the context on your latency targets (p95 <= 220ms for chat flows) and the throughput load (burst to ~60 concurrent users during peak). Quick recap + recommended next steps: 

- Goal: Replace current in-house reranker + QA assistant with a single Redwood endpoint that meets your latency SLOs while reducing per-token cost.
- Recommended initial model candidates for evaluation: Llama-2-13B (FP16, baseline), Mistral-7B (AWQ 4-bit), and Falcon-40B (GPTQ 4-bit) — chosen to span cost/quality/throughput tradeoffs.
- Why these: Mistral-7B AWQ gives large throughput gains on T4/A10-style instances; GPTQ on Falcon-40B tends to preserve higher instruction-following quality on long-context prompts. FP8 (experimental) can further reduce token compute but has noticeable quality variance on code-like or structured outputs.

Action items
1) We will run a targeted eval using your prompt set (the 120 prompts you shared) across the three model variants — output quality + latency + token cost.
2) I'll send preliminary benchmark artifacts and a short tradeoff doc (quantization notes + recommended runtime config).
3) Set a tech deep-dive next week for Lukas to walk through KV-cache tuning and batching policies.

Attached: prompt set you uploaded (will use for eval), baseline eval harness.

Thanks —

Hi Daniel / Olivia —

Great questions. Quick plan and what we'll deliver by EOD tomorrow (artifacts attached):

Eval plan
- Priority ordering: customer-service (40) -> transaction QA (30) -> misc (50). We'll run all three model variants and produce:
  - Automated metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, Exact-Match where applicable, and a custom relevance score tuned to your domain.
  - Latency and p95/p99 token timing under your target concurrency (we'll replay a subset of traffic to approximate load).
  - Cost per 1000 tokens using Redwood runtime telemetry and predicted Dedicated pricing.

Quantization notes (high-level)
- AWQ (4-bit): Pros — substantial throughput and memory reductions, generally stable on decoder-only models for conversational QA. Cons — can introduce tokenization-level truncation on very long system prompts; we'll flag these cases.
- GPTQ (4-bit): Pros — tends to retain higher fidelity for instruction-following and complex composition (good for transactional templates). Cons — slower encode/decode on some older kernels; may need FP16 fallback for a small percent of prompts.
- FP8 (experimental in our runtime): Pros — best theoretical throughput on Ampere+ GPUs when supported. Cons — greater variability; we recommend canarying FP8 only after human spot-check passes.

What you'll get (attached)
- ri-quantization-tradeoffs-v1.pdf — short trade study with example prompt diffs and guidance.
- eval-results-fintechcorp-20260714.csv — automated metrics across prompts/models.
- fintech-promptset-v2.zip — the prompt set used.

Next steps
- Lukas to schedule a 45-min tech deep-dive (KV-cache, batching, and runtime knobs). Lukas — can you do Thu 16th 10-11am PT or Fri 17th 9-10am PT?
- We'll tag any prompts that show >5% regression in relevance score for human review.
- If AWQ shows acceptable quality on the customer-service set, we'll propose a canary rollout on a small percentage of traffic with automatic FP16 fallback.
